title: Inference burn, batching & hosting fit - intake with Silverpine Health
summary: Initial cost/unit economics intake for Silverpine's patient summarization and triage workloads. Covered per-token pricing sensitivity, batching and KV caching levers, pilot scope, residency/SOC2 and early timelines. Redwood AE + SE aligned on running a short pilot (2-4 weeks) to collect token profiles and throughput targets; security will review SOC2 docs and KMS options.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) fit
next_steps: Redwood to send pilot scope template and pricing scenarios (Maya)
Silverpine to share typical prompt/response traces and peak qps target (Lena/Omar)
Security team to review SOC2 artifact link and KMS options (Priya)
Schedule pilot kickoff for week of 07/28 if traces received
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pilot scope + example pricing worksheet (due 2025-07-18)
Lena Morales & Omar Haddad: Export 1 week of anonymized prompt/response traces + 95th qps estimate (due 2025-07-22)
Priya Shah: Provide list of required compliance artifacts and KMS constraints (due 2025-07-21)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:08] Lena (Silverpine): Hi I'm Lena, head of ML. We own the triage models. Sorry about the slightly late start.
[00:12] Omar (Silverpine): Omar, infra/platform, I look after CI/CD and where the models run.
[00:16] Priya (Silverpine): Priya, security and compliance.
[00:18] Eli (Silverpine): Eli, product, small note taker.
[00:21] Maya: Great. Arjun is our SE and will walk through some technical tradeoffs. Arjun?
[00:27] Arjun (Redwood): Hi all. Quick agenda: understand your workload (prompt shapes, qps, latency SLOs), show cost levers—per-token, batching, KV cache—and map hosting fit: hosted, dedicated, private/VPC.
[00:41] Lena: Quick context — two main flows: one, patient summarization (long context ~1.5k tokens in) and two, triage question answering (short prompts but high qps). The triage is the kicker — maybe 60 to 120 qps peak per region.
[00:58] Omar: Our constraint is budget and also that PHI touches the payload, so residency and encryption matters.
[01:06] Priya: We need SOC2 reports, audit logs, and KMS/HSM options. SSO via SAML is required.
[01:14] Maya: Totally. We see that often. On cost, quick question: are you primarily focused on unit cost (per token) or overall monthly spend cap?
[01:23] Eli: Both. We have a hard monthly cap for pilot — around $8k — and we want to understand what that buys for expected qps.
[01:30] Arjun: Ok, two different levers. Per-token price determines marginal cost, but batching, KV prefix caching (we sometimes call it "KV cash" in notes), and model quantization change tokens processed and effective latency.
[01:43] Lena: Can you explain prefix caching? we heard it reduces repeated context cost.
[01:47] Arjun: Sure, prefix or KV cache stores prior attention keys for long contexts. For summarization, if you have repeated patient history patterns or repetitive system prompts, you can avoid re-encoding and cut per-request tokens. Depends on prompt reuse. If you do chunked summarization with overlap you can see 20-60% reduction in average tokens.
[02:04] Omar: Is that automatic on hosted? or requires code changes?
[02:07] Arjun: Redwood does automatic KV caching for compatible model variants in hosting. For dedicated/private we can also enable it, but it needs compatible runtime config and may require pinning a model variant.
[02:17] Lena: What about batching? our triage flow needs sub-200ms latency ideally.
[02:22] Arjun: Batching groups parallel requests to improve throughput and lower per-token cost. But for sub-200ms end-to-end, aggressive batching can add latency. Redwood has adaptive batching — it will batch when it can meet latency SLOs. The unit-econ win depends on batch size; for example, for a 1.3B-ish model you might get 1.8x token throughput at small batch sizes, but for larger models it's more significant.
[02:42] Eli: Any numbers you can ballpark for per-token cost on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:46] Maya: Ballpark only — hosted per-token is usually higher because of multi-tenant margins and flexible routing. Dedicated reserved capacity lowers per-token by 20-40% depending on commit and model. Private/VPC pricing is enterprise and varies — often similar to dedicated after infra amortization.
[03:02] Lena: We're also considering an on-prem airgapped compliance later — will Redwood support that?
[03:07] Arjun: Yes, Redwood Private can be packaged for on-prem; it requires more lead time and licensing. For pilots we recommend hosted or dedicated pilot first to validate workload and collect traces.
[03:18] Priya: About encryption and keys — do you support customer-managed keys?
[03:22] Maya: Yes KMS/HSM integrations supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports CMEK for some plans and we can discuss an enterprise arrangement for full BYOK.
[03:31] Omar: Ok, for the triage flow — 60-120 qps target, mean payload ~60 tokens in and 40 tokens out. If we kept it on hosted, will we hit the $8k cap?
[03:43] Arjun: Quick calc: 100 qps sustained for a month is large — multiply tokens: 100 req/s * (60+40)=100*100=10k tokens/s = 864M tokens/day — that's obviously huge so likely we're looking at bursts or much lower sustained. Are you sure about sustained numbers?
[04:03] Lena: No, that's peak concurrent. Sustained average is more like 6 qps with peaks at 100 for short periods.
[04:09] Arjun: That changes things. Pilot budgeting typically looks at token distribution and peak slices. If average is 6 qps, hosted with batching and caching for the summarization might fit $8k for a short pilot, but we need traces to be sure.
[04:21] Maya: This is why we ask for a week of traces — prompt shapes, 95th percentile qps, and typical prompt length. That lets us run the cost worksheet.
[04:29] Eli: We'll get that.
[04:31] Priya: For SOC2, do you have a shareable link to artifacts?
[04:34] Maya: Yes, I'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs. Also the audit log examples and SAML setup doc.
[04:40] Lena: Back to batching — if adaptive batching is in play, are some requests prioritized? like urgent queries?
[04:46] Arjun: Yes, Redwood supports priority lanes. You can set a low-latency route for urgent requests (which will bypass batch queues or use smaller batches) and a throughput lane for cheaper processing. There's also routing by cost tier — cheaper model variants for non-critical requests.
[05:00] Omar: How much complexity is it to maintain two lanes? our developers worry about orchestration complexity.
[05:05] Arjun: We expose APIs and SDK flags; it's lightweight. You'd tag requests with a priority field and the routing layer handles it. The console also surfaces per-route cost and latency so ops can tune.
[05:16] Lena: Do you have any recommendations for chunking our long summaries to maximize KV cache hit rates?
[05:20] Arjun: Chunk boundaries that align with clinical sections tend to help — e.g., history, meds, allergies — and reuse system prompts. Also store stable context (templates) in the KV so repeated tokens are cached. We'll share a short doc with best practices.
[05:33] Eli: Competitor question — we evaluated Anthropic model and they showed decent latency but higher token burn for summarization, is that consistent?
[05:40] Maya: Different models have different tokenization and generation behavior. Token burn depends on output verbosity and repetition. Redwood's pricing is model-agnostic but effective unit cost changes with model selection and quantization.
[05:51] Omar: For dedicated, what's the lead time and commitment?
[05:54] Maya: Dedicated pools usually need a 30–60 day lead time for provisioning, and commit levels typically start at monthly reserved capacity; discounts depend on commit length.
[06:03] Priya: For private on-prem, what is the typical SLA and support model?
[06:07] Arjun: Private deployments are negotiated — you get control plane ops support, dedicated support SLA, and integration assistance. The SLA depends on the package.
[06:16] Lena: I'm worried about noisy neighbors in hosted affecting our tail latency during triage spikes.
[06:21] Arjun: We have SLO-backed routing and can pin you to Dedicated or reserve burst capacity; for hosted we also offer priority lanes and burst guarantees on some tiers.
[06:32] Eli: If we did a short pilot on hosted to validate waveform and then move to dedicated, what data do you need from us to simulate cost for dedicated?
[06:39] Arjun: Week of traces (token counts, timestamps), expected concurrency profiles, and target latency SLOs. With that we run workload simulation and propose reserve sizing and a cost delta.
[06:50] Maya: Also tell us which features require residency or private storage. That changes whether we can use hosted or need VPC.
[06:56] Priya: We'll flag PHI content and need VPC encryption and retention rules — data must be retained 90 days then purged by default.
[07:05] Maya: Noted.
[07:08] Lena: A practical question — what quantization or model variants do you recommend for summarization vs triage?
[07:14] Arjun: For short high-qps triage, smaller quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) on modern transformer families often hit your latency goals and lower cost. For long summarization where quality-sensitive, use higher-precision variants or larger models but exploit KV caching to reduce repetitive compute.
[07:30] Omar: Are there any gotchas with prefix cache when we have redactions or patient IDs mixed into prompts?
[07:36] Arjun: If prompts contain sensitive unique tokens, caching must be aware. We can mask PII before caching or set cache policies to avoid storing unique tokens. That is part of deployment config.
[07:47] Priya: Good. We'll need to confirm redaction tooling.
[07:50] Maya: Redwood has integrations and we can recommend a pipeline.
[07:54] Eli: Timeline — if we hand over traces this Friday, can we get pilot pricing and proposal next week?
[07:59] Maya: Yes, we'll aim for a one-week turnaround for a scoped pilot and pricing table.
[08:05] Arjun: We'll also include a simulated token burn projection across hosted/dedicated/private options.
[08:11] Lena: About cost projections, do you include KV cache savings in the worksheet or is that a follow-up after pilot results?
[08:16] Arjun: We'll provide estimated ranges based on typical hit rates. But real hit rates are workload-dependent; the pilot gives actual numbers and then we refine.
[08:25] Omar: Any example number for cache hit rate? say for clinical summaries?
[08:29] Arjun: Industry experience: if you reuse a lot of boilerplate (system prompts and templates), 20–60% token reduction. If not much reuse, it's low. We'll capture in the worksheet a low/median/high scenario.
[08:43] Priya: Security nuance — audit log retention requirements, can we export logs to our SIEM?
[08:48] Maya: Yes, we support pushing audit logs to customer endpoints or S3, and can integrate with common SIEMs.
[08:55] Lena: One more — what's the typical per-token delta between hosted and dedicated for the kinds of models we discussed?
[08:59] Maya: Very roughly 20–40% cheaper on dedicated depending on commit. We'll show exact deltas in the pricing scenarios.
[09:08] Eli: Ok, that seems reasonable.
[09:11] Maya: Recap of action items: We will send SOC2 docs, pilot scope template, pricing worksheet; you will send traces and compliance artifacts. Plan to reconvene after you share traces and we return a proposal.
[09:24] Lena: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:27] Priya: Thank you.
[09:29] Maya: We'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kickoff targets. Bye all.
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors, e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache and speaker overlap at times. References to 'hosted/dedicated/private' are shorthand for Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private respectively. Security will review SOC2 and KMS docs shared via link.
